jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.description:
Location

Brookfield Place - 181 Bay Street

Business - Energy

Brookfield Energy operates one of the world’s largest publicly traded platforms for sustainable energy. Our energy portfolio consists of hydroelectric, wind, utility-scale solar, distributed generation and storage facilities in North America, South America, Europe and Asia. Our operating capacity totals over 35,000 megawatts and our development pipeline stands at approximately 200,000 megawatts. Our portfolio of sustainable solutions assets includes our investments in Westinghouse (a leading global nuclear services business) and a utility and independent power producer with operations in the Caribbean and Latin America, as well as both operating assets and a development pipeline of carbon capture and storage capacity, agricultural renewable natural gas and materials recycling.

Brookfield Energy is the flagship listed energy company of Brookfield Asset Management, a leading global alternative asset manager with over $1 trillion of assets under management.

To learn more about the Brookfield Energy group, visit https://www.brookfield.com/about-us/capabilities/energy.

Brookfield Culture

Brookfield has a unique and dynamic culture. We seek team members who have a long-term focus and whose values align with our Attributes of a Brookfield Leader: Entrepreneurial, Collaborative and Disciplined. Brookfield is committed to the development of our people through challenging work assignments and exposure to diverse businesses.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities

Review quarterly and annual financial statements and reports in accordance with IFRS;
Prepares and assesses support used for the management discussion and analysis sections of the quarterly and annual reports and investor supplemental;
Leads the finance workstream relating to debt and equity security issuances initiated by the capital markets team by collaborating with internal and external stakeholders;
Assists with the annual budgeting process and ad hoc financial planning and analysis requests;
Provides assistance with ad hoc investor relations requests and annual investor day;
Has a skeptical mindset and wiliness to continuously learn to further understanding of accounting standards, business performance and industry trends;
Analyzes results and data received with skepticism and critical thinking to ensure it meets the appropriate financing reporting requirements and a willingness to challenge others as needed;
Directs the research, interpretation, and application of new accounting standards/guidelines to assess potential impacts on financial reporting activities including the financial statements and reporting structure;
Manage the external audit process including the corporate finance team during quarterly reviews and annual external audits to meet various deadlines;
Modifies existing and/or designs new processes that maximize operational efficiency including the implementation of new technology;
Owns internal controls for the financial reporting process to meet SOX requirements;
Fulfill ad hoc projects to assist with information requests, including for senior management and rating agencies;
Commitment to the development of the finance team through coaching and opportunities to promote an environment of continuous learning.

Key Requirements / Qualifications

Professional designation: CA or CPA with 6–10 years of progressively senior experience in accounting or finance, including 2–3 years of people leadership.
Technical expertise: Experience with consolidation software (e.g., OneStream) and familiarity with XBRL; background in renewable energy or asset management is considered an asset.
Business & analytical acumen: Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and ability to translate complex financial information into clear insights.
Communication & negotiation: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to explain complex issues clearly and use tact, diplomacy, and strong negotiation skills to influence and build alignment.
Leadership & collaboration: Demonstrated leadership capability, initiative, and the ability to build and maintain strong working relationships across all levels and with external stakeholders. Committed to team collaboration and to developing finance team members through effective coaching.
Problem-solving & reporting: Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to gather, analyze, and synthesize data into concise and meaningful reports.
Interpersonal effectiveness: Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively across diverse groups and functions.

Position Opening Reason:

Backfill

Brookfield is committed to maintaining a Positive Work Environment that is safe and respectful; our shared success depends on it. Accordingly, we do not tolerate workplace discrimination, violence or harassment.

Brookfield is committed to creating an accessible and inclusive organization. We are committed to providing barrier-free and accessible employment practices in compliance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act. Should you require a Human Rights Code-protected accommodation through any stage of the recruitment process, please make them known when contacted and we will work with you to meet your needs.

jobs.title: Director, Derivatives Post Trade Technology
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 260446

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Role

The Director, Derivatives Post
‑
Trade Technology
is responsible for the strategic direction, leadership, and oversight of global Derivatives Post‑Trade Technology with primary accountability for Confirmations, Settlements, and post trade lifecycle processing
across OTC and listed derivatives.

This role drives modernization of the derivatives post‑trade technology landscape, partnering closely with Global Wholesale Operations, Risk, Finance, Legal, and regional Technology teams. The incumbent will define and execute a technology strategy that reduces operational and settlement risk, improves straight‑through processing, enhances regulatory compliance, and delivers measurable business value.

Is this role right for you? In this role you will:

Own the end ‑ to ‑ end technology stack supporting derivatives confirmations and settlements , including trade confirmation, matching, affirmation, settlement instruction generation, and exception management.
Provide strategic leadership for post‑trade processing across OTC and exchange‑traded derivatives, including rates, FX, credit, and equity derivatives.
Drive modernization initiatives focused on automation, straight‑through processing (STP), resiliency, and reduction of manual controls and operational risk.
Ensure 24x7 production stability for critical derivatives post‑trade platforms with global follow‑the‑sun support.
Lead delivery of medium to large technology programs with annual IT spend typically ranging from $2MM to $15MM.
Manage complex regulatory and industry‑driven initiatives (e.g., T+1/T+0 settlement impacts, margin and settlement alignment, recordkeeping and audit requirements).
Partner with Operations and business stakeholders to translate derivatives post‑trade requirements into actionable technology roadmaps and executable delivery plans.
Own and manage vendor relationships across the derivatives post‑trade ecosystem (e.g., confirmation, matching, settlement, and messaging platforms).
Apply modern engineering and delivery practices including Agile, DevOps, CI/CD, cloud‑adjacent architectures, and automation frameworks.
Ensure adherence to enterprise architecture standards, information security policies, and data governance requirements.
Act as the primary technology interface between derivatives Operations, Product Control, Risk, and other Capital Markets Technology teams.
Lead continuous improvement initiatives to strengthen incident management, root‑cause analysis, and knowledge transfer for production issues.
Communicate technology strategy, risk posture, and delivery status effectively to senior technology and business leadership.
Understand how the Bank’s risk appetite and risk culture should be considered in day-to-day activities and decisions.
Creates an environment in which their team pursues effective and efficient operations of their respective areas in accordance with Scotiabank’s Values, its Code of Conduct and the Global Sales Principles, while ensuring the adequacy, adherence to and effectiveness of day-to-day business controls to meet obligations with respect to operational, compliance, AML/ATF/sanctions and conduct risk.
Builds a high-performance environment and implements a people strategy that attracts, retains, develops and motivates their team by fostering an inclusive work environment and using a coaching mindset and behaviors; communicating vision/values/business strategy; and, managing succession and development planning for the team.

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We’d love to work with you if you have:

12+ years of technology and capital markets experience, with senior leadership accountability.
Strong technical background in post‑trade, settlements, or confirmations technology.
Deep understanding of derivatives lifecycle processing, particularly confirmations, settlements, and exception management.
Proven experience delivering large‑scale, complex technology programs in a regulated environment.
Strong vendor management and commercial negotiation experience.
Excellent business acumen and ability to align technology delivery to strategic and financial objectives.
Demonstrated ability to lead transformation, continuous improvement, and operational resilience initiatives.
Exceptional communication skills with the ability to engage executive leadership and senior business stakeholders.

What's in it for you?

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Allyship - We strive to create an inclusive culture where every employee is empowered to reach their fullest potential, respected for who they are, and are embraced through bias-free practices and inclusive values across Scotiabank. We embrace diversity and provide opportunities for all employee to learn, grow & participate through our various Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) that span across diverse gender identities, ethnicity, race, age, ability & veterans.
Accessibility and Workplace Accommodations - We value the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the Bank and are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Scotiabank continues to locate, remove, and prevent barriers so that we can build a diverse and inclusive environment while meeting accessibility requirements.
Upskilling through online courses, cross-functional development opportunities, and tuition assistance.
Competitive Rewards program including bonus, flexible vacation, personal, sick days, and benefits will start on day one.
Community Engagement - no matter where you choose to work from; we offer opportunities for community engagement & belonging with our various programs.

Location(s): Canada : Ontario : Toronto

Scotiabank is a leading bank in the Americas. Guided by our purpose: "for every future", we help our customers, their families and their communities achieve success through a broad range of advice, products and services, including personal and commercial banking, wealth management and private banking, corporate and investment banking, and capital markets.

At Scotiabank, we value the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the Bank, and are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. If you require accommodation (including, but not limited to, an accessible interview site, alternate format documents, ASL Interpreter, or Assistive Technology) during the recruitment and selection process, please let our Recruitment team know. If you require technical assistance, please click here. Candidates must apply directly online to be considered for this role. We thank all applicants for their interest in a career at Scotiabank; however, only those candidates who are selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Finance Director (6 month contract)
jobs.description:
This is a 6 month contract with permanent potential at the end of the contract

About the Opportunity

Lead the preparation and review of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements in accordance with IFRS
and applicable regulatory requirements.
Oversee the financial reporting process
, ensuring accurate, timely, and complete reporting to senior management, the Board, and other stakeholders.
Manage the year-end audit process
, serving as the primary contact for external auditors and coordinating the preparation of audit schedules and supporting documentation.
Ensure appropriate application and interpretation of new and evolving IFRS standards
, assessing their impact on the organization and implementing required changes.
Oversee technical accounting matters
, including complex transactions, revenue recognition, leases, financial instruments, consolidations, and other IFRS-related issues.
Develop and maintain accounting policies, procedures, and internal controls
to ensure compliance with IFRS and promote the integrity of financial reporting.
Lead the month-end and quarter-end close processes
, identifying opportunities to improve reporting accuracy, efficiency, and timeliness.
Review financial results and provide variance analysis and financial insights
to senior leadership, highlighting key business drivers, risks, and opportunities.
Oversee the preparation of management reporting, financial analysis, budgets, forecasts, and financial models
to support strategic decision-making.
Lead, mentor, and develop the finance and accounting team
, fostering a high-performing environment with strong accountability, technical expertise, and continuous improvement.

General Financial Oversight:
Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements and reports, highlighting key metrics and trends.
Assist in developing financial policies, procedures, and internal controls to streamline financial operations.
Work closely with senior leadership to support business decisions and optimize financial performance.
Assist in preparing for audits, including providing necessary documentation for revenue and payroll audits.
Ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations regarding payroll and revenue recognition.

Process Improvement:
Continuously assess and improve payroll and revenue recognition processes to increase efficiency, accuracy, and compliance.
Identify and implement automation opportunities to streamline payroll processing and financial reporting.
Collaborate with IT and software vendors to maintain and optimize payroll and accounting systems.

Skills
Exceptional attention to detail with a high level of accuracy.
Strong problem-solving abilities and analytical skills.
Ability to communicate complex financial information clearly to both financial and non-financial stakeholders.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
Advanced proficiency in Excel (pivot tables, v-lookups, etc.).

About You

CPA or other relevant certifications preferred.
5+ years of experience in accounting or finance, with a focus on IFRS reporting.
Strong knowledge of IFRS
and experience preparing and reviewing complex financial statements and disclosures.
Experience leading external audits and working effectively with external auditors and other key stakeholders.
Proven experience managing month-end, quarter-end, and year-end financial reporting processes
.
Strong understanding of revenue recognition principles (ASC 606 or equivalent).
Solid understanding of accounting principles and regulatory requirements

jobs.title: Director Consulting, Business Transformation & AI
jobs.description:
Position Description

Artificial Intelligence is reshaping every industry, transforming how organizations operate, innovate, and create value. But organizations aren't looking for more technology. They're looking for trusted advisors who can help them modernize operations, transform how work gets done, and realize measurable business outcomes.

At CGI, we're building on decades of consulting excellence, proven AI capabilities, and global innovation to help clients navigate this transformation. We're looking for a business consulting leader who can help expand that capability while influencing how we continue to bring AI enabled business transformation to market.

As Canada's largest IT and business consulting services firm, and a global leader with more than 400 offices worldwide, CGI combines the entrepreneurial spirit of a local business with the strength, scale, and expertise of a global organization. We call our employees Partners for a reason: 90% are shareholders who take ownership of our success. Here, you'll have the autonomy to influence strategy, the resources to make an impact, and the opportunity to help shape the future of consulting.

Your Role: Lead Transformation. Shape Strategy. Enable Growth.

As a Director Consulting, Business Transformation & AI, you'll serve as a senior business transformation consultant and trusted advisor, helping organizations understand how AI can create practical, measurable business value and realize sustainable value from their AI investments.

Working alongside CGI's Directors of Consulting Services, you'll bring deep expertise in business transformation and AI to strengthen client relationships, shape strategic opportunities, and guide organizations through complex transformation initiatives. Rather than owning client accounts, you'll complement our account leaders by helping clients develop transformation strategies, modernize business processes, and accelerate responsible AI adoption.

You'll also help shape the continued evolution of CGI's Business Transformation & AI consulting capabilities across the Atlantic Business Unit. Building on CGI's established consulting practice, global AI expertise, and proven client success, you'll have the opportunity to influence our strategy, evolve consulting offerings, strengthen our market presence, and help define how we continue delivering AI enabled transformation for our clients.

You'll collaborate closely with CGI's technical AI specialists, architects, and delivery teams, serving as the bridge between client business objectives and successful implementation.

If you're passionate about business transformation, executive advisory services, emerging technologies, and helping organizations prepare for what's next, we'd love to hear from you.

Your future duties and responsibilities

Client Leadership & Strategic Advisory

Serve as a trusted advisor to client stakeholders, business leaders, technology leaders, and executives on business transformation, AI adoption, and digital modernization.
Lead executive workshops that help organizations define transformation priorities, AI strategies, investment roadmaps, and measurable business outcomes.
Advise clients on operating model redesign, organizational change, Responsible AI, governance, and workforce transformation.
Build trusted relationships with key client stakeholders, decision makers, and influencers, strengthening CGI's position as a trusted transformation partner.

Opportunity Shaping & Business Development

Provide business transformation and AI expertise that strengthens client relationships and shapes strategic opportunities.
Support executive presentations, discovery workshops, proposals, business cases, and transformation roadmaps.
Collaborate across CGI consulting, engineering, cloud, cybersecurity, data, and account and delivery teams to recommend and shape integrated client solutions.
Bring innovative thinking, market insight, and consulting expertise to strategic pursuits and client engagements.

Practice Leadership & Thought Leadership

Help shape and evolve CGI's Business Transformation & AI consulting capabilities across the Atlantic Business Unit.
Contribute to consulting methodologies, reusable assets, market offerings, executive workshops, and leading practices.
Mentor consultants and help build AI fluency across CGI's consulting Partner community.
Represent CGI through conferences, executive forums, industry events, and thought leadership initiatives while staying current on emerging business and technology trends.

Solution Leadership

Translate client business challenges into practical transformation opportunities enabled by AI and digital technologies.
Connect clients with the right CGI capabilities, technical specialists, delivery teams, and alliance partner solutions.
Help ensure consulting engagements deliver measurable business outcomes and long term client value.

Required Qualifications To Be Successful In This Role

12+ years of experience in management consulting, business transformation, digital transformation, technology consulting, or advisory services.
Demonstrated success advising organizations on complex business transformation initiatives and translating emerging technologies into measurable business outcomes.
Strong understanding of Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI, Data & Analytics, Digital Transformation, and the evolving technology landscape.
Demonstrated executive presence with the ability to influence senior client stakeholders, facilitate strategic discussions, and build trusted relationships.
Experience supporting business development through executive advisory, opportunity shaping, proposals, workshops, and strategic consulting engagements.
Comfortable collaborating with technical AI specialists and delivery teams without needing to be the primary solution developer.
Exceptional communication, facilitation, presentation, and relationship building skills.
Degree in Business, Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Familiarity with Responsible AI, AI governance, enterprise transformation, and organizational change management.

Asset Qualifications

MBA or graduate degree in Business, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Organizational Change, or a related discipline.
Certifications in AI, Cloud, Business Architecture, Digital Transformation, Change Management, or related disciplines.
Experience working with public sector, healthcare, credit unions, financial services, utilities, or other regulated industries.
Bilingualism (English/French) is considered an asset.
Willingness to travel within Canada and internationally as required (travel estimated at 25% and primarily within Atlantic Canda).

CGI is providing a reasonable estimate of the pay range for this role. The determination of this range includes factors such as skill set level, geographic market, experience and training, and licenses and certifications. Compensation decisions depend on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is $100,000–$190,000. This role is an existing vacancy.

Together, as owners, let’s turn meaningful insights into action.

Life at CGI is rooted in ownership, teamwork, respect and belonging. Here, you’ll reach your full potential because…

You are invited to be an owner from day 1 as we work together to bring our Dream to life. That’s why we call ourselves CGI Partners rather than employees. We benefit from our collective success and actively shape our company’s strategy and direction.

Your work creates value. You’ll develop innovative solutions and build relationships with teammates and clients while accessing global capabilities to scale your ideas, embrace new opportunities, and benefit from expansive industry and technology expertise.

You’ll shape your career by joining a company built to grow and last. You’ll be supported by leaders who care about your health and well-being and provide you with opportunities to deepen your skills and broaden your horizons.

At CGI, we value the strength that diversity brings and are committed to fostering a workplace where everyone belongs. We collaborate with our clients to build more inclusive communities and empower all CGI partners to thrive. As an equal-opportunity employer, being able to perform your best during the recruitment process is important to us. If you require an accommodation, please inform your recruiter.

That same commitment to fairness extends to how we use technology. To support our recruitment team, AI tools may be used to help assess applications though they never replace human judgement. All hiring decisions remain entirely in the hands of our recruitment professionals.

To learn more about accessibility at CGI, contact us via email. Please note that this email is strictly for accessibility requests and cannot be used for application status inquiries.
